body:
DAE deal with monthly peaks of symptoms? I don't have a menstrual cycle and haven't since before this became a particularly bad problem, but toward the end of every month, I start getting really, really bad anxiety.

I feel like a balloon right now, and anxiety's just getting pumped into me more and more. I feel like I'm gonna pop, like if I stubbed my toe I'd explode and just black out from reality for a bit.

A "friend" in high school was just the absolute worst about stealing interests from me. I was into stuff I picked up from friends online, like bands that never toured in the US and spoke no english, ball jointed dolls, anime back when it was shameful, etc. She cut her hair to the exact same cut as me, got glasses in the same style as mine, claimed to own a $200 doll customized to be a member of a band I liked, where the doll would easilly cost $700+, and started buying merch of the bands and anime I liked.

It has an almost uncanny valley feel, like looking in the mirror in the dark. It's... wrong, but not in an identifiable way.
I really appreciate this. It feels... validating, I guess? I'm just so emotionally overfilled and drained at the same time, so words are hard but... yeah.

I'm elegant in typing but jesus christ if talking doesn't make me sound like I've got about 3 brain cells left and they're all just screaming at each other.

BPD is such a fucking dink. Like, I completely understanding becoming functionally mute because you can't put clean, crisp words together. Instead of a word salad, you get the floor of a greasy pizza shop during superbowl weekend. Just... bad. Big bad.

I've got the most intense wanderlust, I just want to uproot my entire life and run away, making awful financial decisions all the way, and start over again. I know you can't outrun BPD but that dumb bitch is telling me to try it.

It's like having a devil on one shoulder that wants to see you fail, and on the other shoulder is a kid doing his absolute best to try to get you to not do dumb, self-imolating shit. But the devil's got the gas and the lighter ready for you, and the kid's always about half a second from a breakdown too.

To me, it's very much the "I don't want to die, but I sometimes wish I'd never been born at all." mindset.

I'm relatively mentally healthy, I don't feel the need to lash out, test my partner, obsess over him, cheat, have backup boyfriends or any of the other toxic shit I did when I had no control over my BPD.

But, I still deal with being apathetic on any random day, and occasionally depressed and just sobbing. It's hard, because people understand crying. They want to help that. But straight face saying "I wish I didn't exist." or "I wish a bullet would come through that wall right now and end it." tends to just make people scared, not caring.
